declared_purpose: Protect files used with openclaw through local version indexing, modification rollback and deletion recovery. Explicit requirements include text diffs/snapshots, full binary/trash copies, user confirmation, 7/14-day retention and confirmed cleanup (SKILL.md:1-25, 61-68, 117-129, 265-307).

data_operations.data_scope: Python version returned by the prescribed version command.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Invoking agent through local command output.
data_operations.condition: The entry document requires this check before operations; missing Python stops the skill without dependency installation.

data_operations.operation: Initialize local storage and persist the operation index
data_operations.source: Runtime home directory, caller-supplied roots and generated operation records
data_operations.data_scope: Storage directories and logs containing file/artifact paths, actions, summaries, counts, timestamps, expiry, importance and retention.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Default ~/.openclaw/minivcs/, or caller-selected vcs_root; logs.json is written through a temporary JSON file and replacement.
data_operations.condition: Construction creates missing storage. Index operations read and rewrite the shared log. No project partition is implemented.

data_operations.operation: Classify selected paths and inspect file format
data_operations.source: Selected file path, expanded home path and selected file bytes
data_operations.data_scope: Path-based importance inference determines 7/14-day retention. Modify reads the first 1 KB for NUL-based binary classification. Configured path segments cause tracking to be skipped.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local process; inferred importance and retention enter the index and operation result.
data_operations.condition: Modify/delete check existence and exclusions first. Binary inspection applies to modify; importance matching does not enumerate credential directories.

data_operations.source: Entire selected file and its previous stored baseline
data_operations.data_scope: Current text, three-line-context diff, full current baseline and full nonempty previous baseline as snapshot. Reading falls back to UTF-8 decoding with invalid bytes ignored.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local process and diffs/, bases/, snapshots/ beneath vcs_root.
data_operations.condition: Non-skipped modify classified as text. A first record writes an all-addition diff and baseline without a snapshot. Unchanged nonempty baselines skip new artifacts. The agent is required to obtain confirmation first.

data_operations.data_scope: Entire file and copy2-preserved metadata; byte size enters the summary and return value.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local backups/ directory, operation index and calling process.
data_operations.condition: Binary modify makes a full copy while retaining the original. A warning above 50 MiB is returned after copying. Agent instructions require prior agreement to local storage and confirmation before further similarly large backups.

data_operations.operation: Move a deleted file into recoverable local storage
data_operations.data_scope: Full file; trash filename contains a timestamp and original basename. Original and trash paths enter the index.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local trash/ directory; original location is vacated by shutil.move.
data_operations.condition: record_delete performs the move directly. Agent instructions require confirmation of local storage, including explicit agreement for binary files.

data_operations.operation: Restore or roll back stored content
data_operations.source: Record-selected trash file, text snapshot or binary backup
data_operations.data_scope: Full restored content and updated action/restoration timestamps.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Recorded absolute target or current project_root joined with the recorded relative path; updated logs.json.
data_operations.condition: Restore requires an applicable record and existing artifact. Trash restoration moves its copy; text restoration writes the snapshot; binary restoration copies the backup. Text snapshots and binary backups remain stored. Repeated restoration is rejected.

data_operations.operation: Return history, differences and cleanup information
data_operations.source: Shared operation index and requested patch files
data_operations.data_scope: History defaults to ten records; file history matches the relative/absolute path string. Cleanup returns complete expired records. Diff API returns the full patch; CLI diff display prints its first 30 lines.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Python caller or CLI stdout. Agent instructions require reporting operation results and expired-record lists to the user; no further recipient is implemented.
data_operations.condition: Explicit history/trash/expiry queries, or automatic cleanup queries after successful record operations and unchanged nonempty text checks. Global history and cleanup are not project-filtered.

data_operations.source: Record timestamps, inferred retention and current time
data_operations.data_scope: Expiry timestamps and expired-record selection; requested extension adds one retention cycle to the existing expiry.
data_operations.condition: Expiry is a cleanup eligibility timestamp, not automatic deletion. RESTORED and ROLLED_BACK records are excluded from ordinary expiry queries. Extension requires an explicit call.

data_operations.operation: Remove records and associated local artifacts
data_operations.source: Specified record IDs or records selected by cleanup
data_operations.data_scope: Index entries, patches, trash copies, snapshots and binary backups; baseline removal is conditional.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local filesystem through os.remove and rewritten logs.json.
data_operations.condition: remove or per-record deletion removes artifacts by default. cleanup --confirm selects ordinary due records. A baseline is removed only when deleting a MODIFY record with no other MODIFY records for that path. APIs do not independently enforce consent or expiry.

data_operations.source: Records older than a caller-selected number of days
data_operations.data_scope: Matching index entries and, optionally, their patch files; snapshots, trash, binary backups and baselines are not removed by this path.
data_operations.condition: clean_expired or expired <days> --clean; --delete-files enables patch deletion only. Selection uses creation age rather than each record's expireAt.

data_operations.operation: Merge modification history through the Python API
data_operations.source: MODIFY records matching a file's path string
data_operations.data_scope: Discarded record entries and their patches/snapshots; selected record and baseline remain.
data_operations.condition: merge_modify requires multiple MODIFY records and keeps the latest by default or a specified matching record.

potential_excess.data_scope: Another project's prior contents and metadata when projects share a relative file path.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: The new operation's diff/snapshot in the shared store, file-history caller, or restoration target under the current project_root.
potential_excess.condition: Projects use the same vcs_root and matching relative paths. Baselines and file-history matching lack project identity; relative restore targets use the current project root.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Per-file rollback and recovery require the correct file's history. Global cleanup scanning is explicitly required, but cross-project content substitution is an implementation consequence.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Keep complete version information associated with its originating file and preserve the required global expiry scan.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Namespace baselines and record lookups by project identity; verify the originating project or obtain an explicit restore destination.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Continue supporting absolute paths, requested global history and full-table cleanup without silently mixing relative-path identities.

potential_excess.data_scope: Expired restored-record metadata, rolled-back snapshots/patches and binary backups; potentially unreferenced text baselines.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: logs.json, snapshots/, diffs/, backups/ and bases/ under vcs_root.
potential_excess.condition: Successful restoration changes the action to RESTORED or ROLLED_BACK, which ordinary cleanup excludes. Copies retained after rollback can therefore persist beyond expiry. Removing a final ROLLED_BACK record also bypasses the MODIFY-only baseline cleanup.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Restoration is necessary; exclusion from retention cleanup is an implementation choice beyond the declared 7/14-day, user-confirmed retention workflow.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Restore the target and prevent duplicate restoration while retaining protection data only under an applicable retention decision.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Include expired completed records in cleanup confirmation and remove their artifacts and unreferenced baselines when approved.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve restored target files, user-controlled extensions and confirmation before deleting protection data.

potential_excess.data_scope: Full snapshots, deleted-file copies, binary backups and baselines whose index entries have been removed.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: snapshots/, trash/, backups/ and bases/ under vcs_root.
potential_excess.condition: Compatibility expired --clean deletes matching index entries. Even with --delete-files, it removes only patches, leaving other content outside indexed cleanup.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The relevant purpose is expired-history cleanup. Orphaning protection copies is an implementation defect rather than required recovery behavior.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Remove the approved history and requested physical artifacts consistently, while preserving artifacts still needed by retained records.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Route physical compatibility cleanup through complete per-record deletion. For intentional metadata-only cleanup, retain an artifact manifest and explicit retention handling.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Respect the physical-deletion option and retained-record dependencies; do not silently delete copies requested to remain.

potential_excess.data_scope: Up to ten existing records' paths, actions, summaries, timestamps, expiry and importance.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: CLI stdout and its calling agent.
potential_excess.condition: The Step 1 history command is executed solely to initialize storage; it queries shared history without a file filter.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Initialization requires creating storage, which construction already performs automatically. The history query is a redundant action for this purpose.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Initialize the local directories and index.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Initialize during the first requested operation or provide silent initialization.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Continue returning history when the user actually requests it; no remote disclosure is established by this output.

potential_excess.data_scope: Expired records' artifact paths, summaries and change counts beyond the required cleanup-list fields.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Python caller through due_for_cleanup; no onward recipient is shown.
potential_excess.condition: Automatic record results return complete expired record dictionaries.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The full expiry scan and user-facing cleanup list are required. Returning every stored field is extra data within that required action.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Identify expired records and let the user choose deletion or extension.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Return ID, file path, action, creation/expiry times and importance; retrieve artifact paths only for requested artifact operations.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve the complete scan, expiry ordering and all information needed for cleanup confirmation.

unknowns: The invoking host's transport, provider access and retention of normal returns or user messages are undocumented. No remote disclosure is implemented in the supplied source.
Actual user confirmation and cleanup execution cannot be established from source. Consent is an agent instruction; Python operations do not enforce it.
Host-level permissions, encryption, external backup/sync and recoverability after filesystem removal are unspecified. File removal does not establish secure erasure.
